decisions.context: The classifier processes millions of documents daily, with seasonal volume swings and multiple downstream teams. The brief does not require request-time results.
decisions.rationale: Scheduled batch scoring fits the stated large daily volume and shared consumption. Sources including “How to power up your product by machine learning with python microservice, pt. 1” describe batch deployment; the checked design point was unattested, so this is a reasoned choice rather than a documented combination.
consequences: Processing capacity must accommodate seasonal peaks.

decisions.context: Document volume changes considerably over the year, so capacity needs to follow workload. The brief does not specify latency or cost targets.
decisions.rationale: Elastic scaling addresses the explicit seasonal workload swings; the rival scale-to-zero choice may be less suitable when high-volume scoring needs ready capacity. “Architecting a Machine Learning Pipeline: How to build scalable Machine Learning systems - Part 2/2” discusses elastic resources. The checked combination was unattested.
consequences: Peak throughput still needs sizing and observation.

decisions.context: Several teams consume the classifier’s results, so the system needs a stable way to expose them. The brief does not specify each team’s integration pattern.
decisions.rationale: REST provides a broadly consumable interface for the several teams named in the brief. “How to power up your product by machine learning with python microservice, pt. 1” documents API-backed model services; the checked combination was unattested.
consequences: Teams integrate through a shared prediction contract.
Service availability and interface changes need operational ownership.

decisions.context: Operators need visibility when classification quality drifts. Drift can be observed from input changes and measured from predictions when labeled outcomes become available.

alternatives.label: Input and feature-drift monitoring
cons: Input shifts do not prove quality loss

decisions.rationale: Choose input-drift monitoring for timely operator visibility, and treat it as a signal to investigate rather than proof of quality decline. “Productionizing Machine Learning with a Microservices Architecture” describes monitoring feature processes and values. The checked point warned that multiple monitoring values are not exclusive, so monitoring practices can be combined where labels permit.
consequences: Operators receive drift signals for investigation.
Quality assessment depends on labeled outcomes, whose availability is unspecified.

decisions.context: Drift response may lead to model updates, and candidate classifiers need a quality check before deployment. The brief does not define an evaluation metric or acceptance threshold.
decisions.rationale: Held-out offline evaluation gives a pre-deployment quality gate for any update. “Architecting a Machine Learning Pipeline: How to build scalable Machine Learning systems - Part 2/2” documents candidate evaluation; the point check flagged that workflow coordination should be decided first, and its combination was unattested.
consequences: The brief must define labels, metrics, and acceptance thresholds.

decisions.context: Drift investigations and safe updates benefit from linking deployed models to their training data and runs. Multiple teams also need reproducible classification behavior.
decisions.rationale: Comprehensive traceability best supports explaining drift and reproducing candidate updates across teams. “Continuous Intelligence: Moving Machine Learning Application into Production Reliably” and “MLOps Principles” document end-to-end lifecycle records; the checked point was unattested.
consequences: Record dataset, pipeline, run, model, and deployment metadata.
Teams take on additional tracking and governance work.

uncovered: Workflow execution coordination and orchestration (flagged as a prerequisite by the evaluation decision).
Data retention, privacy, and access controls for insurance documents.
Label acquisition and delay, evaluation metrics, and promotion thresholds.
Consumer-specific delivery, availability, and freshness requirements.
Model choice, including whether the LLM classifier is hosted or self-managed.
